source.text: Ἦν δὲ τὸ πάσχα καὶ τὰ ἄζυμα μετὰ δύο ἡμέρας.

records.literal_gloss: It was now the Passover and the Unleavened [Bread] after two days.

en.L: Now it was the Passover and the [Feast of] Unleavened Bread after two days.
en.B: Two days remained before the Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread.
en.R: In two more days it would be time for the Passover and the Festival of Unleavened Bread.

vi.L: Bấy giờ, hai ngày sau là Lễ Vượt Qua và [Lễ] Bánh Không Men.
vi.B: Còn hai ngày nữa là đến Lễ Vượt Qua và Lễ Bánh Không Men.
vi.R: Hai ngày nữa là đến Lễ Vượt Qua và Lễ Bánh Không Men.

ko.L: 그런데 유월절과 무교[절]이 이틀 뒤였다.
ko.B: 유월절과 무교절을 이틀 앞둔 때였다.
ko.R: 이틀이 지나면 유월절과 무교절, 곧 누룩 없는 빵을 먹는 명절이 시작될 참이었다.

es.L: Era la Pascua y [la fiesta de] los Panes sin Levadura dentro de dos días.
es.B: Faltaban dos días para la Pascua y la fiesta de los Panes sin Levadura.
es.R: Dentro de dos días iba a ser la Pascua y la fiesta de los Panes sin Levadura.

fr.L: Or la Pâque et [la fête des] Pains sans levain étaient dans deux jours.
fr.B: La Pâque et la fête des Pains sans levain devaient avoir lieu deux jours plus tard.
fr.R: Dans deux jours, ce serait la fête de la Pâque et des Pains sans levain.

sw.L: Basi ilikuwa Pasaka na [Sikukuu ya] Mikate Isiyotiwa Chachu baada ya siku mbili.
sw.B: Zilikuwa zimebaki siku mbili kabla ya Pasaka na Sikukuu ya Mikate Isiyotiwa Chachu.
sw.R: Baada ya siku mbili ingekuwa wakati wa Pasaka na Sikukuu ya Mikate Isiyotiwa Chachu.

pt.L: Ora, dali a dois dias era a Páscoa e os [Pães] sem Fermento.
pt.B: Faltavam dois dias para a Páscoa e a festa dos Pães sem Fermento.
pt.R: Dali a dois dias ia ser a Páscoa e a festa dos Pães sem Fermento.

am.L: ፋሲካና የቂጣ [በዓል] ከሁለት ቀን በኋላ ነበር።
am.B: ፋሲካና የቂጣ በዓል ሊደርሱ ሁለት ቀን ቀርቶ ነበር።
am.R: የፋሲካና እርሾ ያልገባበት ቂጣ የሚበላበት በዓል ሊደርስ ሁለት ቀን ብቻ ቀርቶ ነበር።

decisions.choice: the Passover and Unleavened Bread: one festival week
decisions.reason: The Passover meal was eaten on the night of 15 Nisan and was followed by seven days of eating bread without yeast (Exodus 12:1-20; Leviticus 23:5-6). By this time the two names were used together for the whole festival.

decisions.choice: after two days: two days from now
alternatives: two full days later, on the third day
decisions.reason: The phrase counts forward from the time Mark is describing; it places the plot of 14:1-2 just before the feast.

decisions.choice: Festival of Unleavened Bread
decisions.reason: Readable uses "festival", an everyday word for a holy feast.

decisions.choice: "Lễ Vượt Qua" and "Lễ Bánh Không Men"
alternatives: "Lễ Bánh Không Men" unbracketed at Literal
decisions.reason: "Lễ Vượt Qua" is the Vietnamese John's name for the Passover; the second feast takes the usual Protestant name. The Greek says only "the Unleavened [Bread]", so Literal brackets "Lễ" (feast) there, as the English brackets "Feast of".

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean; the narrative honours Jesus with "께서" and -시-, Jesus speaks in the plain style (해라체), the disciples speak to him in 합쇼체, Jesus prays to the Father in 합쇼체, and Mark's historic presents stay present only at Literal ("말한다", "말씀하신다", "온다"), through chapter 14
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change (style guide, sections 4 and 7). Literal keeps Mark's present tense in narrative (14:12-13, 14:17, 14:27, 14:30, 14:32-34, 14:37, 14:41, 14:43, 14:45, 14:51, 14:53, 14:61, 14:63, 14:66-67); Balanced and Readable use the past, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "무교[절]" (L); "무교절" (B); "무교절, 곧 누룩 없는 빵을 먹는 명절" (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek says only "the unleavened [things]"; "무교절" is the established Korean name of the feast, and Literal brackets the "절" (feast) the Greek leaves out. Readable explains the name once.

decisions.choice: los Panes sin Levadura
decisions.reason: The usual Spanish name of the feast; Literal brackets "la fiesta de", which the Greek leaves out.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (B), with Literal keeping Mark's present tense ("disent", "envoie", "vient", "arrive" ...); passé composé (R); speech in the passé composé at every level
alternatives: passé composé for narration at every level
decisions.reason: The French brief for narrative: Balanced narrates in the passé simple, the tense of written narrative; Readable uses the passé composé, as French is spoken today; Literal keeps the historic present wherever Mark has it (14:12, 13, 17, 27, 30, 32, 33, 37, 41, 43, 45, 51, 53, 63, 66), as the English Literal does.

decisions.choice: la Pâque; [la fête des] Pains sans levain (L); la fête des Pains sans levain (B, R)
decisions.reason: "La Pâque" as in the French of John. "Les Azymes" is a learned word few readers know; "Pains sans levain" says what was eaten, and Literal brackets "la fête des", which the Greek leaves out.

decisions.choice: Mikate Isiyotiwa Chachu; [Sikukuu ya] bracketed at Literal
decisions.reason: The Greek says only 'the unleavened [breads]'. Swahili names the feast by what was eaten, bread made without yeast ('chachu'); Literal brackets 'Sikukuu ya' (the Feast of), as the English brackets 'Feast of'. The same name in 14:12.

decisions.choice: "ፋሲካ" (Passover); "የቂጣ በዓል" (the Feast of Unleavened Bread, L, B); "እርሾ ያልገባበት ቂጣ የሚበላበት በዓል" (the feast when bread made without yeast is eaten, R)
decisions.reason: "ቂጣ" is flat bread baked without yeast, so "የቂጣ በዓል" names the feast plainly; Readable says what the bread is, as in Matthew 26:17.

source.text: καὶ ἐζήτουν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς πῶς αὐτὸν ἐν δόλῳ κρατήσαντες ἀποκτείνωσιν, ἔλεγον γάρ· Μὴ ἐν τῇ ἑορτῇ, μήποτε ἔσται θόρυβος τοῦ λαοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And were seeking the chief priests and the scribes how him by deceit having seized they might kill. \v 2 They were saying for, Not during the feast, lest there will be an uproar of the people.

en.L: And the chief priests and the scribes were seeking how they might seize {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} by deceit [and] kill [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}]. \v 2 For they were saying, "Not during the feast, or there will be an uproar of the people."
en.B: The chief priests and the scribes were looking for a way to take {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} by a trick and put {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to death. \v 2 For they kept saying, "Not at the feast, in case the people raise an uproar."
en.R: The leading priests and the teachers of God's law were trying to find a secret way to arrest Jesus and kill {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \v 2 They said, "We must not do it during the festival. The crowds might start a riot."

vi.L: Và các thầy tế lễ cả và các thầy thông giáo tìm cách dùng mưu bắt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} để giết. \v 2 Vì họ nói: "Đừng [làm] trong kỳ lễ, kẻo dân chúng sẽ náo loạn."
vi.B: Các thầy tế lễ cả và các thầy thông giáo tìm cách dùng mưu bắt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và giết đi. \v 2 Vì họ cứ bảo nhau: "Đừng làm trong kỳ lễ, kẻo dân chúng gây náo loạn."
vi.R: Các thầy tế lễ cả và các thầy dạy luật đang tìm cách bí mật bắt Đức Giê-xu và giết {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. \v 2 Họ nói: "Chúng ta không được làm việc này trong kỳ lễ, kẻo dân chúng nổi loạn."

ko.L: 그리고 대제사장들과 율법학자들은 어떻게 하면 속임수로 그분을 붙잡아 죽일 수 있을지 찾고 있었다. \v 2 그들이 "명절 동안에는 안 된다. 백성 가운데 소동이 일어날지도 모른다" 하고 말하고 있었기 때문이다.
ko.B: 대제사장들과 율법학자들은 꾀를 써서 예수를 붙잡아 죽일 방법을 찾고 있었다. \v 2 그들은 "명절에는 안 된다. 백성이 소동을 일으킬지도 모른다" 하고 말했다.
ko.R: 대제사장들과 율법학자들은 아무도 모르게 예수를 붙잡아 죽일 방법을 찾고 있었다. \v 2 그들은 "명절에는 그렇게 하지 말자. 사람들이 폭동을 일으킬지도 모른다" 하고 말했다.

es.L: Y los principales sacerdotes y los escribas buscaban cómo prenderlo con engaño y matar[lo]. \v 2 Porque decían: «No durante la fiesta, no sea que haya un alboroto del pueblo».
es.B: Los jefes de los sacerdotes y los escribas buscaban la manera de apresarlo con un engaño y darle muerte. \v 2 Porque decían: «Durante la fiesta no, no sea que el pueblo se alborote».
es.R: Los jefes de los sacerdotes y los maestros de la ley buscaban una manera secreta de arrestar a Jesús y matarlo. \v 2 Decían: «No debemos hacerlo durante la fiesta. La gente podría armar un alboroto».

fr.L: Et les chefs des prêtres et les scribes cherchaient comment, {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ayant saisi par ruse, ils [{{deity_pronoun:le|Le}}] tueraient. \v 2 Car ils disaient : « Pas pendant la fête, de peur qu’il y ait du tumulte dans le peuple. »
fr.B: Les chefs des prêtres et les scribes cherchaient un moyen de s’emparer de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} par une ruse et de {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} faire mourir. \v 2 Car ils se disaient : « Pas pendant la fête, sinon le peuple risque de se soulever. »
fr.R: Les chefs des prêtres et les spécialistes de la Loi cherchaient un moyen secret d’arrêter Jésus et de {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} tuer. \v 2 Ils disaient : « Il ne faut pas le faire pendant la fête. La foule pourrait se révolter. »

sw.L: Na wakuu wa makuhani na waandishi walikuwa wakitafuta jinsi ambavyo wangemkamata kwa hila [na] kumwua. \v 2 Kwa maana walikuwa wakisema, "Si wakati wa sikukuu, isije ikatokea ghasia ya watu."
sw.B: Wakuu wa makuhani na waandishi walikuwa wakitafuta njia ya kumkamata kwa hila na kumwua. \v 2 Kwa maana walikuwa wakisemezana, "Tusifanye hivyo wakati wa sikukuu, watu wasije wakafanya fujo."
sw.R: Viongozi wa makuhani na walimu wa sheria walikuwa wakitafuta njia ya siri ya kumkamata Yesu na kumwua. \v 2 Walisema, "Tusifanye jambo hili wakati wa sikukuu. Umati wa watu unaweza kuanzisha ghasia."

pt.L: E os chefes dos sacerdotes e os escribas procuravam como prendê-{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} com astúcia [e] matá-{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}. \v 2 Pois diziam: "Não durante a festa, senão haverá tumulto do povo."
pt.B: Os chefes dos sacerdotes e os escribas procuravam um jeito de prendê-{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} por meio de alguma artimanha e matá-{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}. \v 2 Pois diziam: "Não durante a festa, para que o povo não se revolte."
pt.R: Os chefes dos sacerdotes e os mestres da Lei estavam procurando um jeito de prender Jesus em segredo e matá-{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}. \v 2 Eles diziam: "Não podemos fazer isso durante a festa. O povo pode começar uma revolta."

am.L: የካህናት አለቆችና ጸሐፍትም እንዴት በተንኮል ይዘው እንደሚገድሉት ይፈልጉ ነበር፤ \v 2 «የሕዝቡ ሁከት እንዳይነሣ በበዓሉ አይሁን።» ይሉ ነበርና።
am.B: የካህናት አለቆችና የሕግ መምህራን ኢየሱስን በዘዴ ይዘው የሚገድሉበትን መንገድ ይፈልጉ ነበር። \v 2 ነገር ግን፦ «ሕዝቡ እንዳያምፅ በበዓሉ ጊዜ አይሁን።» ይሉ ነበር።
am.R: የካህናት አለቆችና የሕግ መምህራን ኢየሱስን በድብቅ ይዘው የሚገድሉበትን መንገድ ይፈልጉ ነበር። \v 2 እንዲህም አሉ፦ «ይህን በበዓሉ ጊዜ ማድረግ የለብንም። ሕዝቡ ሁከት ሊያስነሣ ይችላል።»

decisions.choice: by deceit: by a trick, out of public view
decisions.reason: The word means cunning or treachery. They want to seize Jesus quietly, away from the crowds who listened to him gladly (12:37).

decisions.choice: the feast: Passover week, when Jerusalem was full of pilgrims
alternatives: the meal on the first night only
decisions.reason: Large crowds came for the festival, and the Romans feared unrest at this time. An arrest in public could start a riot.

decisions.choice: they were saying: they kept saying among themselves
alternatives: they said it once in public
decisions.reason: The tense describes talk that went on while they made their plans.

decisions.choice: leading priests; teachers of God's law
decisions.reason: The same Readable terms as in earlier chapters.

decisions.choice: "các thầy tế lễ cả" (L, B, R); "các thầy thông giáo" (L, B), "các thầy dạy luật" (R)
decisions.reason: The Protestant terms used in the Vietnamese John (11:47; 8:3) and settled in the style guide; Readable says plainly what the scribes did. "Thượng tế" and "kinh sư" are the Catholic words. The same forms are used through the chapter, with "các trưởng lão" for the elders (14:43, 14:53).

decisions.choice: "대제사장들", "율법학자들" at every level, Readable included, through chapter 14
decisions.reason: "대제사장들" is the Korean John's word (11:47) and "율법학자들" the Korean Mark 3:22 and John 8:3 word; both are plain enough for Readable, which says what the English Readable spells out ("leading priests", "teachers of God's law"). "서기관" is the older church word.

decisions.choice: los principales sacerdotes (L), los jefes de los sacerdotes (B, R); los escribas (L, B), los maestros de la ley (R)
decisions.reason: The titles used in the Spanish of John (7:32; 18:3) for the chief priests; Readable says what the scribes were, teachers of the law. These choices hold throughout the chapter (14:10, 43, 53, 55).

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans on every pronoun for Christ or God
alternatives: stressed pronouns only, as in the Spanish of John
decisions.reason: By the book-wide rule for Mark set at 1:2: every pronoun Spanish writes for Christ or God takes the deity_pronoun setting, whether stressed (él, mí, ti, tú), possessive (su, mi, tu) or an object pronoun before the verb (le, lo, me, te). A pronoun at the start of a sentence, or joined to the end of a verb ("prenderlo", "matarlo"), is written plain.

decisions.choice: les chefs des prêtres (every level); les scribes (L, B), les spécialistes de la Loi (R)
decisions.reason: The terms of the French of John: "les chefs des prêtres" at every level, kept distinct from "le grand prêtre" (14:47, 53); "les scribes" at Literal and Balanced, and "les spécialistes de la Loi" at Readable (John 8:3), where the English Readable says "teachers of God's law". The same in 14:43 and 14:53.

decisions.choice: wakuu wa makuhani (L, B), viongozi wa makuhani (R); waandishi (L, B), walimu wa sheria (R)
alternatives: walimu wa sheria at every level
decisions.reason: As in John (7:32; 8:3; 18:3): 'waandishi' is the established Swahili name for the scribes, and Readable says what they did, as the English Readable says 'teachers of God's law'; 'sheria' is lowercase, as the style sheet asks. The same in 14:10, 14:43, 14:53 and 14:55.

decisions.choice: os chefes dos sacerdotes; os mestres da Lei
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 26:3: "os chefes dos sacerdotes" already says who they were, so Readable keeps the settled term where the English Readable says "leading priests"; for the scribes it says "os mestres da Lei" (style section 6).

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans: the suffixes for Jesus ("እንደሚገድሉት") stay as they are
alternatives: a span on each pronoun, as the English has
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the reader setting that capitalises pronouns for God and Christ has nothing to change in Amharic; the pronouns and suffixes for Jesus stay as they are and the Amharic has no deity_pronoun spans (docs/amharic-style.md, section 7).

decisions.choice: "የካህናት አለቆች" (chief priests) at every level; "ጸሐፍት" (scribes, L), "የሕግ መምህራን" (teachers of the Law, B, R)
decisions.reason: The scribes were teachers of the Law, not copyists, so Balanced and Readable say so; Literal keeps the traditional word (docs/amharic-style.md, section 6). "የካህናት አለቆች" is already plain Amharic and serves at Readable too.

source.text: Καὶ ὄντος αὐτοῦ ἐν Βηθανίᾳ ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ Σίμωνος τοῦ λεπροῦ κατακειμένου αὐτοῦ ἦλθεν γυνὴ ἔχουσα ἀλάβαστρον μύρου νάρδου πιστικῆς πολυτελοῦς· συντρίψασα τὴν ἀλάβαστρον κατέχεεν αὐτοῦ τῆς κεφαλῆς.

records.literal_gloss: And being him in Bethany in the house of Simon the leper, reclining him, came a woman having an alabaster flask of perfumed oil of nard pure, very costly; having broken the alabaster flask she poured [it] on his head.

en.L: And while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was in Bethany in the house of Simon the leper, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was reclining [at table], a woman came having an alabaster flask of perfumed oil, pure nard, very costly; breaking the alabaster flask, she poured [it] over {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} head.
en.B: Jesus was in Bethany, at the home of Simon the leper. While {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} lay at the meal, a woman came with an alabaster flask of pure nard, a perfumed oil of great value. She broke the flask and poured the oil over {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} head.
en.R: Jesus was in the town of Bethany, eating a meal at the home of Simon. Simon had once had a bad skin disease. A woman came in with a jar made of fine white stone. It was full of very costly perfume made from nard. She broke the jar open and poured the perfume on Jesus' head.

vi.L: Và khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ở Bê-tha-ni, trong nhà Si-môn người phung, lúc {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đang ngả mình [bên bàn ăn], có một người phụ nữ đến, mang theo một bình thạch cao đựng dầu thơm cam tùng nguyên chất, rất đắt giá; cô đập vỡ bình thạch cao và đổ [dầu] trên đầu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu đang ở Bê-tha-ni, tại nhà Si-môn, người bị phung. Khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đang ngồi dùng bữa, có một người phụ nữ đến, mang theo một bình thạch cao đựng dầu thơm cam tùng nguyên chất, rất quý giá. Cô đập vỡ bình và đổ dầu trên đầu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu đang ở làng Bê-tha-ni. Ngài đang ăn tại nhà một người tên là Si-môn. Ông này trước kia từng mắc một bệnh ngoài da nặng. Có một người phụ nữ bước vào, mang theo một cái bình làm bằng đá trắng quý. Trong bình đầy dầu thơm rất đắt tiền làm từ cây cam tùng. Cô đập vỡ bình và đổ dầu thơm lên đầu Đức Giê-xu.

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 베다니에서 나병 환자 시몬의 집에 계셨는데, [식탁에] 기대어 앉아 계실 때에, 한 여자가 매우 값진 순수한 나드 향유가 든 설화석고 병을 가지고 왔다. 그 여자는 그 설화석고 병을 깨뜨려 [향유를] 그분의 머리에 부었다.
ko.B: 예수께서 베다니에 있는 나병 환자 시몬의 집에 계셨다. 예수께서 식탁에 앉아 계실 때에, 한 여자가 매우 값진 순수한 나드 향유가 든 설화석고 병을 가지고 왔다. 그 여자는 병을 깨뜨리고 향유를 예수의 머리에 부었다.
ko.R: 예수께서 베다니라는 마을에서 시몬의 집에 계셨다. 시몬은 전에 심한 피부병을 앓던 사람이었다. 예수께서 식사를 하고 계실 때, 한 여자가 들어왔다. 그 여자는 하얀 돌로 만든 병을 들고 있었다. 병에는 나드로 만든 아주 비싼 향유가 가득 들어 있었다. 그 여자는 병을 깨뜨려 열고, 향유를 예수의 머리에 부었다.

es.L: Y estando {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} en Betania, en la casa de Simón el leproso, mientras estaba recostado [a la mesa], vino una mujer que tenía un frasco de alabastro de perfume de nardo puro, muy costoso; rompiendo el frasco de alabastro, {{deity_pronoun:se|Se}} lo derramó sobre la cabeza.
es.B: Jesús estaba en Betania, en casa de Simón el leproso. Mientras estaba recostado a la mesa, llegó una mujer con un frasco de alabastro lleno de nardo puro, un perfume de gran valor. Rompió el frasco y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} derramó el perfume sobre la cabeza.
es.R: Jesús estaba en el pueblo de Betania, comiendo en casa de Simón. Simón había tenido una enfermedad grave de la piel. Llegó una mujer con un frasco hecho de una piedra blanca y fina. Estaba lleno de un perfume de nardo muy caro. Ella rompió el frasco y derramó el perfume sobre la cabeza de Jesús.

fr.L: Et comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était à Béthanie, dans la maison de Simon le lépreux, alors qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était allongé [à table], une femme vint, ayant un flacon d’albâtre de parfum de nard pur, très coûteux ; ayant brisé le flacon d’albâtre, elle [le] versa sur {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} tête.
fr.B: Jésus était à Béthanie, chez Simon le lépreux. Pendant qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était à table, une femme arriva avec un flacon d’albâtre rempli d’un parfum de nard pur, de grande valeur. Elle brisa le flacon et versa le parfum sur {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} tête.
fr.R: Jésus était dans le village de Béthanie. Il prenait un repas chez Simon. Ce Simon avait eu autrefois une grave maladie de peau. Une femme est entrée avec un flacon fait d’une belle pierre blanche. Il était plein d’un parfum de nard qui coûtait très cher. Elle a cassé le flacon et elle a versé le parfum sur la tête de Jésus.

sw.L: Na alipokuwa Bethania katika nyumba ya Simoni mwenye ukoma, alipokuwa ameegemea [mezani], alikuja mwanamke mwenye chupa ya alabasta ya manukato, nardo safi, ya thamani kubwa; akaivunja chupa ya alabasta, akayamimina juu ya kichwa {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}}.
sw.B: Yesu alikuwa Bethania, nyumbani kwa Simoni mwenye ukoma. Alipokuwa ameegemea mezani akila, mwanamke mmoja alikuja na chupa ya alabasta yenye nardo safi, manukato ya thamani kubwa. Akaivunja chupa hiyo, akayamimina manukato kichwani {{deity_pronoun:pake|Pake}}.
sw.R: Yesu alikuwa katika mji wa Bethania, akila chakula nyumbani kwa Simoni. Simoni aliwahi kuwa na ugonjwa mbaya wa ngozi. Mwanamke mmoja aliingia na chupa iliyotengenezwa kwa jiwe jeupe zuri. Ilikuwa imejaa manukato ya bei ghali sana yaliyotengenezwa kwa nardo. Akaivunja chupa, akayamimina manukato kichwani pa Yesu.

pt.L: E, estando {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} em Betânia, na casa de Simão, o leproso, estando {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} reclinado [à mesa], veio uma mulher que tinha um frasco de alabastro de unguento de nardo puro, muito caro; quebrando o frasco de alabastro, ela [o] derramou sobre a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} cabeça.
pt.B: Jesus estava em Betânia, na casa de Simão, o leproso. Enquanto {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} estava à mesa, chegou uma mulher com um frasco de alabastro cheio de nardo puro, um óleo perfumado de grande valor. Ela quebrou o frasco e derramou o óleo na cabeça {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}.
pt.R: Jesus estava na cidade de Betânia, comendo na casa de Simão. Simão já tinha tido uma doença de pele grave. Uma mulher entrou com um vaso feito de uma pedra branca e fina. O vaso estava cheio de um perfume muito caro, feito de nardo. Ela quebrou o vaso e derramou o perfume na cabeça de Jesus.

am.L: እርሱም በቢታንያ በለምጻሙ በስምዖን ቤት ሳለና [በማዕድ] ተደግፎ ሳለ፣ እጅግ ውድ የሆነ ንጹሕ የናርዶስ ሽቱ ያለበት የአልባስጥሮስ ብልቃጥ የያዘች አንዲት ሴት መጣች፤ የአልባስጥሮሱንም ብልቃጥ ሰብራ በራሱ ላይ አፈሰሰችው።
am.B: ኢየሱስ በቢታንያ፣ ቀድሞ የቆዳ በሽታ ታሞ በነበረው በስምዖን ቤት ነበር። በማዕድ ተቀምጦ ሳለ አንዲት ሴት እጅግ ውድ የሆነ ንጹሕ የናርዶስ ሽቱ የያዘ የአልባስጥሮስ ብልቃጥ ይዛ መጣች። ብልቃጡንም ሰብራ ሽቱውን በራሱ ላይ አፈሰሰችው።
am.R: ኢየሱስ ቢታንያ በምትባል ከተማ ነበረ። ስምዖን በሚባል ሰው ቤት እየበላ ነበር። ስምዖን ቀድሞ ክፉ የቆዳ በሽታ ይዞት ነበር። አንዲት ሴት ወደ ቤቱ ገባች። ከሚያምር ነጭ ድንጋይ የተሠራ ብልቃጥ ይዛ ነበር። ብልቃጡ ናርዶስ ከሚባል ተክል በተሠራ እጅግ ውድ ሽቱ የተሞላ ነበር። ብልቃጡን ሰብራ ሽቱውን በኢየሱስ ራስ ላይ አፈሰሰችው።

decisions.choice: reclining: lying on a couch at a meal
decisions.reason: At a formal meal guests lay on their left side around a low table, with their feet away from it.

decisions.choice: alabaster flask of pure nard: a sealed stone flask of costly perfumed oil
decisions.reason: Alabaster was a soft white stone used for flasks of perfume. Nard was an oil made from a plant that grows in the Himalayas, so it was rare and very costly. The flask was often sealed, so it was broken at the neck to pour out the oil.

decisions.choice: pure: genuine, not mixed with cheaper oils
decisions.reason: The word is rare and its meaning is not certain. The most likely sense is "genuine" or "pure", from a word for trust.

decisions.choice: poured over his head: an anointing like that of a king
decisions.reason: Kings were anointed on the head (1 Samuel 10:1; 2 Kings 9:6). Jesus himself gives the act another meaning in 14:8: it prepares his body for burial.

decisions.choice: the leper (B); had once had a bad skin disease (R)
alternatives: a man with a serious skin disease
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the name by which Simon was known. Readable says what it meant, as in 1:40, and says "had once had" because he was clearly no longer shut out from others. That is an inference.

decisions.choice: a jar made of fine white stone
decisions.reason: Readable explains what alabaster is.

decisions.choice: "ngả mình [bên bàn ăn]" (L); "ngồi dùng bữa" (B); "ăn" (R), also in 14:18
decisions.reason: Guests at a formal meal lay on couches; Literal keeps that picture, while Balanced and Readable use the ordinary Vietnamese way of saying someone is at a meal.

decisions.choice: "người phung" (L, B); "bình thạch cao"; "dầu thơm cam tùng"
decisions.reason: "Phung" is the traditional word for the skin diseases the Greek word covers; Readable describes it, as the English does. "Cam tùng" is nard, as in John 12:3, and "dầu thơm" keeps it an oil. Alabaster is "thạch cao" (Literal and Balanced); Readable describes the stone.

decisions.choice: "설화석고 병" (L, B); "하얀 돌로 만든 병" (R)
decisions.reason: "옥합" is the familiar word of older versions, but it means a jade box; the flask was of alabaster, a soft white stone, which "설화석고" names. "나드 향유" follows the Korean John 12:3.

decisions.choice: "나병 환자" (L, B); "전에 심한 피부병을 앓던" (R)
decisions.reason: "문둥이" is offensive today; "나병 환자" is the established term. Readable says "심한 피부병", since the Greek word covered several skin diseases, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: recostado a la mesa
decisions.reason: Spanish keeps the picture of lying on a couch at a meal (meaning decision m1); Readable says simply that he was eating.

decisions.choice: un parfum de nard pur, as in John 12:3
decisions.reason: "Parfum" is the usual French word for the perfumed oil, as in the French of John 12:3, and it is used through 14:3-8 ("ce parfum").

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on free pronouns and possessives (chake, pake, wangu, nami)
alternatives: a span on every pronoun, as in English
decisions.reason: As in John and the letters: Swahili marks most pronouns for Jesus inside the verb (akamwambia, wakamkamata), and a prefix cannot take a capital, so the Swahili text has fewer setting spans than the English. This holds for the whole chapter.

decisions.choice: ameegemea [mezani] (L), ameegemea mezani (B), akila chakula (R); chupa ya alabasta (L, B), chupa iliyotengenezwa kwa jiwe jeupe (R)
decisions.reason: Guests lay on couches at a meal (meaning decision), so Literal and Balanced say 'kuegemea' (recline), as at 14:18. 'Alabasta' is the soft white stone of the flask; Readable describes it, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: na cabeça {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}
decisions.reason: After "Ela", "sua cabeça" would first be read as the woman's own head, so Balanced says "dele"; Literal keeps "sua", where the clause has Jesus as its subject.

decisions.choice: "ለምጻሙ ስምዖን" (Simon the leper, L), "ቀድሞ የቆዳ በሽታ ታሞ የነበረው" (B, R); "ንጹሕ የናርዶስ ሽቱ" (pure nard perfume); "የአልባስጥሮስ ብልቃጥ" (alabaster flask)
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 26:6-7, Literal keeps the name by which Simon was known and the other levels say what it most likely means; "ብልቃጥ" is a small flask for perfume, not an everyday bottle, and Readable says what alabaster is.

source.text: ἦσαν δέ τινες ἀγανακτοῦντες πρὸς ἑαυτούς· Εἰς τί ἡ ἀπώλεια αὕτη τοῦ μύρου γέγονεν;

records.literal_gloss: Were now some being indignant among themselves: For what this waste of the perfumed oil has happened?

en.L: Now there were some who were indignant among themselves, "Why has this waste of the perfumed oil happened?
en.B: Some of those present were angry and said to one another, "What is the point of wasting this perfume?
en.R: Some of the people there became angry. They said to each other, "Why did she waste that perfume?

vi.L: Nhưng có mấy người tức giận nói với nhau: "Sao lại có sự phí phạm dầu thơm này?
vi.B: Có mấy người ở đó bực tức nói với nhau: "Phí dầu thơm này để làm gì?
vi.R: Có vài người ở đó nổi giận. Họ nói với nhau: "Sao cô ta lại phí dầu thơm ấy như vậy?

ko.L: 그런데 어떤 사람들이 화를 내며 서로 [말했다]. "무엇 때문에 향유를 이렇게 허비하게 되었느냐?
ko.B: 그 자리에 있던 몇 사람이 화가 나서 서로 말했다. "왜 이 향유를 이렇게 낭비하느냐?
ko.R: 거기 있던 몇 사람이 화가 났다. 그들은 서로 말했다. "저 여자가 왜 저 향유를 낭비하느냐?

es.L: Y había algunos que se indignaban entre sí: «¿Para qué se ha hecho este desperdicio del perfume?
es.B: Algunos de los presentes se enojaron y se decían unos a otros: «¿Para qué desperdiciar así este perfume?
es.R: Algunas de las personas que estaban allí se enojaron. Se decían unos a otros: «¿Por qué ha desperdiciado ella ese perfume?

fr.L: Or il y en avait quelques-uns qui s’indignaient entre eux : « Pourquoi cette perte du parfum a-t-elle eu lieu ?
fr.B: Certains de ceux qui étaient là s’indignèrent et se dirent entre eux : « À quoi bon gaspiller ce parfum ?
fr.R: Quelques personnes qui étaient là se sont fâchées. Elles se disaient entre elles : « Pourquoi est-ce qu’elle a gaspillé ce parfum ?

sw.L: Lakini walikuwapo baadhi waliokasirika, [wakisemezana] wao kwa wao, "Kwa nini upotevu huu wa manukato umetokea?
sw.B: Baadhi ya watu waliokuwepo walikasirika, wakaambiana, "Kuna faida gani kupoteza manukato haya?
sw.R: Baadhi ya watu waliokuwa pale walikasirika. Wakaambiana, "Kwa nini ameyapoteza manukato hayo?

pt.L: E havia alguns que estavam indignados entre si: "Para que aconteceu este desperdício do unguento?
pt.B: Alguns dos presentes ficaram irritados e diziam uns aos outros: "Para que desperdiçar este óleo perfumado?
pt.R: Algumas das pessoas que estavam ali ficaram irritadas. Elas diziam umas às outras: "Por que ela desperdiçou esse perfume?

am.L: አንዳንዶች ግን እርስ በርሳቸው እየተቆጡ ነበር፦ «ይህ የሽቱ ብክነት ለምን ሆነ?
am.B: በዚያ ከነበሩት አንዳንዶቹ ተቆጥተው እርስ በርሳቸው እንዲህ ተባባሉ፦ «ይህን ሽቱ እንዲህ ማባከን ምን ይጠቅማል?
am.R: በዚያ የነበሩ አንዳንድ ሰዎች ተበሳጩ። እርስ በርሳቸውም እንዲህ ተባባሉ፦ «ይህን ሽቱ ለምን አባከነችው?

decisions.choice: some: some of those at the meal
decisions.reason: Mark does not say who they were. Matthew 26:8 says the disciples, and John 12:4 names Judas.

decisions.choice: among themselves: to one another, or within themselves
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean they spoke among themselves or felt it inwardly. Since their words are given and they rebuke her in 14:5, they seem to have said it to one another.

decisions.choice: waste: loss, something thrown away
decisions.reason: The word means ruin or loss. To them the oil was simply lost.

decisions.choice: 서로 [말했다] (L)
decisions.reason: The Greek runs straight from "among themselves" into their words; Korean needs a verb of saying, which Literal brackets.

source.text: ἠδύνατο γὰρ τοῦτο τὸ μύρον πραθῆναι ἐπάνω δηναρίων τριακοσίων καὶ δοθῆναι τοῖς πτωχοῖς· καὶ ἐνεβριμῶντο αὐτῇ.

records.literal_gloss: Could for this the perfumed oil have been sold for more than denarii three hundred and have been given to the poor. And they were scolding her.

en.L: For this perfumed oil could have been sold for more than 300 denarii and given to the poor." And they were scolding her.
en.B: It could have fetched more than {{units:a year's wages|300 denarii}}, and the money could have gone to the poor." So they turned on her with harsh words.
en.R: It could have been sold for more than {{units:a year's pay|300 denarii}}. Then the money could have been given to poor people." And they spoke angrily to her.

vi.L: Vì dầu thơm này lẽ ra có thể bán được hơn ba trăm đơ-ni-ê và đem cho người nghèo." Và họ trách mắng cô.
vi.B: Dầu này có thể bán được hơn {{units:một năm tiền công|ba trăm đơ-ni-ê}}, và tiền ấy có thể đem giúp người nghèo." Rồi họ gay gắt trách cô.
vi.R: Dầu ấy có thể bán được hơn {{units:một năm tiền công|ba trăm đơ-ni-ê}}. Rồi lấy tiền đó giúp người nghèo." Và họ nói nặng lời với cô.

ko.L: 이 향유는 삼백 데나리온 이상에 팔려서 가난한 사람들에게 주어질 수 있었다." 그러고는 그 여자를 나무라고 있었다.
ko.B: 이 향유는 {{units:일 년 품삯|300데나리온}}이 넘는 값에 팔 수 있었고, 그 돈을 가난한 사람들에게 줄 수 있었다." 그러면서 그 여자를 몹시 나무랐다.
ko.R: 이 향유를 팔면 {{units:일 년 동안 일해서 버는 돈|300데나리온}}보다 더 많이 받을 수 있었다. 그러면 그 돈을 가난한 사람들에게 줄 수 있었을 것이다." 그리고 그 여자에게 화를 내며 꾸짖었다.

es.L: Porque se podía haber vendido este perfume por más de trescientos denarios y haber dado [el dinero] a los pobres». Y la reprendían.
es.B: Se podría haber vendido por más de {{units:el salario de un año|trescientos denarios}}, y el dinero se podría haber dado a los pobres». Y se volvieron contra ella con duras palabras.
es.R: Se podría haber vendido por más de {{units:el sueldo de un año|trescientos denarios}}. Así se podría haber dado el dinero a los pobres». Y le hablaron con enojo.

fr.L: Car ce parfum aurait pu être vendu plus de trois cents deniers et [l’argent] donné aux pauvres. » Et ils la rudoyaient.
fr.B: On aurait pu le vendre plus de {{units:un an de salaire|trois cents deniers}} et donner l’argent aux pauvres. » Et ils s’en prirent durement à elle.
fr.R: On aurait pu le vendre plus de {{units:un an de salaire|trois cents deniers}}. Et l’argent aurait pu être donné aux pauvres. » Et ils lui ont parlé avec colère.

decisions.choice: 300 denarii: about a year's pay for a worker
decisions.reason: A denarius was a day's wage for a laborer (Matthew 20:2). Three hundred denarii was close to what a worker earned in a year, leaving out Sabbaths and feast days.

decisions.choice: given to the poor: gifts to the poor were expected at Passover
decisions.reason: Giving to the poor was a duty of the law (Deuteronomy 15:11), and it was the custom to give to them at Passover.

decisions.choice: scolding: speaking sternly, with anger
decisions.reason: The verb is the strong one used in 1:43. It means to speak to someone harshly.

decisions.choice: a year's wages (B); a year's pay (R); 300 denarii as the original unit
decisions.reason: The units setting gives a modern sense of the sum by default and the coin as the alternative. Literal keeps the coin.

decisions.choice: {{units:một năm tiền công|ba trăm đơ-ni-ê}} (B, R); "ba trăm đơ-ni-ê" (L)
decisions.reason: As in John 12:5: "đơ-ni-ê" is the established Protestant transliteration of the Roman coin, and the default gives its value in a worker's wages.

decisions.choice: {{units:일 년 품삯|300데나리온}} (B); {{units:일 년 동안 일해서 버는 돈|300데나리온}} (R)
decisions.reason: As in English, Balanced and Readable give the modern sense by default and the original sum as the alternative; Literal keeps "삼백 데나리온", the Korean John's form (12:5).

decisions.choice: {{units:el salario de un año|trescientos denarios}} (B); el sueldo de un año (R)
decisions.reason: The same units span as in the Spanish of John 12:5; Literal keeps the denarii.

decisions.choice: {{units:un an de salaire|trois cents deniers}} (B, R); trois cents deniers (L)
alternatives: un an de salaire, with no setting
decisions.reason: As in the French of John 12:5: the default gives the value a reader can picture (meaning decision m1), and the setting gives the original coin; Literal keeps the coin.

decisions.choice: {{units:o salário de um ano|trezentos denários}}
decisions.reason: As the English: the units setting gives the value of the sum by default and the coin as the alternative; Literal keeps the coin. The number is written in words, as Portuguese writes round hundreds in running text.

decisions.choice: {{units:ከአንድ ዓመት ደመወዝ|ከ300 ዲናር}} (more than a year's wages, more than 300 denarii); Literal keeps "300 ዲናር"
decisions.reason: A denarius was a day's pay for a labourer, so 300 denarii were about a year's wages (m1). A coin has no metric form, so the default gives the value in wages and the alternative the coin, as in Matthew; a sum in birr would date at once. The prefix "ከ-" (more than) goes inside each option because it joins the two differently.

sw.B: Lakini Yesu akasema, "Mwacheni. Kwa nini mnamsumbua?
sw.R: Lakini Yesu akasema, "Acheni kumsumbua. Kwa nini mnamfanyia ugumu?

pt.B: Mas Jesus disse: "Deixem a mulher em paz. Por que vocês a estão incomodando?
pt.R: Mas Jesus disse: "Parem de incomodar a mulher. Por que vocês estão criando problema para ela?

am.L: ኢየሱስ ግን እንዲህ አለ፦ «ተዉአት፤ ለምን ታስቸግሯታላችሁ?
am.B: ኢየሱስ ግን እንዲህ አለ፦ «ተዉአት! ለምን ታስቸግሯታላችሁ?
am.R: ኢየሱስ ግን እንዲህ አለ፦ «አታስቸግሯት! ለምን ታበሳጯታላችሁ?

decisions.choice: causing her troubles: making things hard for her
decisions.reason: The phrase means to bother or harass someone.

decisions.choice: leave her alone: stop what you are doing to her
decisions.reason: The verb can mean "forgive", but here it means to let her be.

decisions.choice: "các con" for those who scolded her, through 14:9
decisions.reason: Vietnamese must choose a relationship that the Greek "you" leaves open. Mark says only "some"; John 12:4 names a disciple, and in Mark Jesus is at a meal with his own, so he is drafted as speaking to them as their teacher. If those who scolded are taken to be other guests, "các người" would fit.

decisions.choice: ustedes / vosotros forms
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to the whole group, so the plural "you" takes the ustedes / vosotros reader setting: ustedes (Latin America, the default) or vosotros (Spain). Every plural "you" in this chapter does the same.

records.literal_gloss: A good work she did to me.

en.L: She has done a good work for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: She has done a beautiful thing for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: a good work: a fine, fitting deed
decisions.reason: The adjective means good and also fine or beautiful. Jewish teaching counted burying the dead among good works, beyond giving to the poor, and 14:8 links her act to burial.

decisions.choice: beautiful
decisions.reason: Balanced brings out the sense of something fine and fitting, not only right.

decisions.choice: por {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}; conmigo (L)
decisions.reason: The stressed "mí" for Christ takes the setting; Literal's "conmigo" is one word and takes none, as in the Spanish of John.

source.text: πάντοτε γὰρ τοὺς πτωχοὺς ἔχετε μεθ’ ἑαυτῶν, καὶ ὅταν θέλητε δύνασθε αὐτοῖς εὖ ποιῆσαι, ἐμὲ δὲ οὐ πάντοτε ἔχετε·

records.literal_gloss: Always for the poor you have with yourselves, and whenever you want you are able to them well to do, me but not always you have.

en.L: For you always have the poor with you, and whenever you want you can do good to them, but you do not always have {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: The poor will be with you at all times, and you can help them any time you wish. But you will not always have {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: There will always be poor people near you. You can help them whenever you want to. But I will not always be here with you.

vi.L: Vì người nghèo thì các con luôn có ở với mình, và bất cứ khi nào muốn, các con đều có thể làm điều tốt cho họ; nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thì các con không có luôn luôn.

vi.R: Lúc nào cũng có người nghèo ở gần các con. Các con có thể giúp họ bất cứ khi nào các con muốn. Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ không ở đây với các con mãi.

ko.L: 가난한 사람들은 늘 너희와 함께 있고, 너희는 원할 때마다 그들에게 잘해 줄 수 있다. 그러나 나는 늘 너희와 함께 있지 않다.
ko.B: 가난한 사람들은 언제나 너희 곁에 있으니, 너희가 원하면 언제든지 그들을 도울 수 있다. 그러나 나는 언제까지나 너희 곁에 있지는 않을 것이다.
ko.R: 가난한 사람들은 언제나 너희 가까이에 있을 것이다. 너희는 원할 때마다 그들을 도와줄 수 있다. 그러나 나는 언제까지나 여기 너희와 함께 있지는 않을 것이다.

es.L: Porque a los pobres siempre los {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y cuando {{plural_you:quieran|queráis}} {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} hacerles bien, pero a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} no siempre {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}}.
es.B: Siempre habrá pobres entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} ayudarlos cuando {{plural_you:quieran|queráis}}. Pero a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} no siempre {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:tendrán|tendréis}}.
es.R: Siempre habrá gente pobre cerca de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. {{plural_you:Pueden|Podéis}} ayudarlos cuando {{plural_you:quieran|queráis}}. Pero yo no estaré siempre aquí con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.

fr.L: Car les pauvres, vous [les] avez toujours avec vous, et quand vous voulez, vous pouvez leur faire du bien ; mais {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, vous ne {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}avez pas toujours.
fr.B: Les pauvres, vous les aurez toujours avec vous, et vous pourrez les aider chaque fois que vous le voudrez. Mais {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, vous ne {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}aurez pas toujours.
fr.R: Il y aura toujours des pauvres près de vous. Vous pourrez les aider quand vous voudrez. Mais {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, je ne serai pas toujours ici avec vous.

sw.L: Kwa maana maskini mnao pamoja nanyi siku zote, na wakati wowote mnapotaka mnaweza kuwatendea mema, lakini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} hamko {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} siku zote.
sw.B: Maskini watakuwa pamoja nanyi wakati wote, na mnaweza kuwasaidia wakati wowote mnaotaka. Lakini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} hamtakuwa {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} siku zote.
sw.R: Siku zote kutakuwa na watu maskini karibu nanyi. Mnaweza kuwasaidia wakati wowote mnaotaka. Lakini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} sitakuwa hapa pamoja nanyi siku zote.

pt.L: Pois sempre vocês têm os pobres com vocês, e, quando quiserem, podem lhes fazer o bem; mas a {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} nem sempre têm.
pt.B: Os pobres sempre estarão com vocês, e vocês podem ajudá-los quando quiserem. Mas a {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} vocês não terão sempre.
pt.R: Sempre vai haver pessoas pobres perto de vocês. Vocês podem ajudá-las quando quiserem. Mas eu não vou estar sempre aqui com vocês.

am.R: ድሆች ሁልጊዜ በአጠገባችሁ ይኖራሉ። በፈለጋችሁ ጊዜ ልትረዷቸው ትችላላችሁ። እኔ ግን ሁልጊዜ እዚህ ከእናንተ ጋር አልኖርም።

decisions.choice: you always have the poor with you: an echo of Deuteronomy 15:11
alternatives: a saying that the poor do not matter
decisions.reason: The law says the poor will never cease from the land, and so Israel must open its hand to them. Jesus does not set aside that duty. He says there will be time for it.

decisions.choice: you will not always have me: Jesus speaks of his coming death
alternatives: he is going on a journey
decisions.reason: The words point ahead to 14:8 and to his death within days.

decisions.choice: I will not always be here with you
alternatives: you do not always have me
decisions.reason: Readable says what the words mean in plain terms.

decisions.choice: "가난한 사람들은 늘 너희와 함께 있고" (L)
alternatives: "너희는 가난한 사람들을 늘 너희와 함께 가지고 있고"
decisions.reason: Korean does not "have" people with it; Literal makes the poor the subject, as the Greek "have with you" means, and keeps the contrast with "나는" at the end.

source.text: ὃ ἔσχεν ἐποίησεν, προέλαβεν μυρίσαι τὸ σῶμά μου εἰς τὸν ἐνταφιασμόν.

records.literal_gloss: What she had she did; she took beforehand to anoint my body for the burial.

en.L: She has done what she could; she has anointed {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} body beforehand for burial.
en.B: She did what was in her power. She has poured perfume on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} body ahead of time, to make it ready for burial.
en.R: She did what she was able to do. She put perfume on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} body to get it ready to be buried. She did it before the time came.

vi.L: Cô ấy đã làm điều cô có thể làm; cô đã xức dầu thân thể {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} trước để tẩm liệm.

ko.L: 그 여자는 할 수 있는 일을 하였다. 장례를 위하여 내 몸에 미리 향유를 부었다.
ko.B: 그 여자는 자기 힘으로 할 수 있는 일을 했다. 내 장례를 위하여 미리 내 몸에 향유를 부어 준비해 둔 것이다.
ko.R: 그 여자는 자기가 할 수 있는 일을 했다. 내가 묻힐 때를 위하여 내 몸에 향유를 부어 준비해 주었다. 그때가 오기 전에 미리 한 것이다.

es.L: Hizo lo que tenía [a su alcance]; se anticipó a ungir {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} cuerpo para la sepultura.
es.B: Hizo lo que estaba en su mano. Ha derramado perfume sobre {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} cuerpo de antemano, para prepararlo para la sepultura.
es.R: Hizo lo que pudo. Puso perfume sobre {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} cuerpo para prepararlo para el entierro. Lo hizo antes de que llegara el momento.

fr.L: Elle a fait ce qu’elle pouvait ; elle a d’avance parfumé {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} corps pour l’ensevelissement.
fr.B: Elle a fait ce qui était en son pouvoir. Elle a d’avance répandu du parfum sur {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} corps pour le préparer à la sépulture.
fr.R: Elle a fait ce qu’elle pouvait faire. Elle a mis du parfum sur {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} corps pour le préparer à être enterré. Elle l’a fait avant le moment venu.

sw.L: Amefanya kile alichoweza; ametangulia kuupaka mwili {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} manukato kwa ajili ya maziko.
sw.B: Amefanya kile kilichokuwa katika uwezo wake. Ameupaka mwili {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} manukato mapema, kuuandaa kwa maziko.
sw.R: Amefanya kile alichoweza kufanya. Ameweka manukato juu ya mwili {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} ili kuuandaa kwa ajili ya kuzikwa. Amefanya hivyo kabla wakati haujafika.

pt.L: Ela fez o que pôde; antecipou-se em ungir o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} corpo para o sepultamento.
pt.B: Ela fez o que estava ao seu alcance. Derramou perfume sobre o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} corpo antes do tempo, para prepará-lo para o sepultamento.
pt.R: Ela fez o que podia fazer. Pôs perfume no {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} corpo para prepará-lo para ser enterrado. Ela fez isso antes da hora.

am.L: የቻለችውን አደረገች፤ ሰውነቴን ለቀብር አስቀድማ ቀባች።
am.B: የምትችለውን አደረገች። ለቀብሬ እንዲዘጋጅ ሰውነቴን አስቀድማ ሽቱ ቀባች።
am.R: የምትችለውን አደረገች። ሰውነቴ ለመቀበር እንዲዘጋጅ ሽቱ ቀባችው። ጊዜው ሳይደርስ አስቀድማ ይህን አደረገች።

decisions.choice: what she had she did: she did what she could
decisions.reason: The phrase means she did all that lay in her power.

decisions.choice: she took beforehand to anoint: she anointed ahead of time
decisions.reason: The verb "take beforehand" with another verb means to do something in advance.

decisions.choice: for burial: the anointing looks ahead to Jesus' death
alternatives: she knew he was about to die
decisions.reason: Bodies were anointed for burial. In 16:1 the women come to anoint his body and find the tomb empty, so this is the only anointing his body receives. Mark does not say whether she understood this.

decisions.choice: "tẩm liệm" (L, B); "chôn cất" (R)
decisions.reason: As in John 12:7: "tẩm liệm" is preparing a body for burial, the sense of the Greek word; Readable uses the everyday word.

decisions.choice: "ሰውነቴ" (my body) here; "ሥጋዬ" at the supper (14:22)
decisions.reason: For the living body that is anointed Amharic says "ሰውነት"; "ሥጋዬ" is kept for the words over the bread, as Matthew does (26:12, 26:26).

source.text: ἀμὴν δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν, ὅπου ἐὰν κηρυχθῇ τὸ εὐαγγέλιον εἰς ὅλον τὸν κόσμον, καὶ ὃ ἐποίησεν αὕτη λαληθήσεται εἰς μνημόσυνον αὐτῆς.

records.literal_gloss: Truly now I say to you, wherever is proclaimed the gospel in the whole world, also what did this [woman] will be spoken for a memorial of her.

en.L: And truly I say to you, wherever the gospel is proclaimed in the whole world, what she has done will also be told in memory of her."
en.B: Truly I tell you, in every place in the whole world where the gospel is proclaimed, people will tell what she has done, and remember her."
en.R: I tell you the truth: The good news will be preached in the whole world. And everywhere it is preached, people will tell what this woman did, and they will remember her."

vi.L: Thật vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các con, bất cứ nơi nào Tin Lành được rao giảng trong khắp thế gian, điều cô ấy đã làm cũng sẽ được kể lại để ghi nhớ cô."
vi.B: Thật vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các con, Tin Lành được rao giảng ở bất cứ nơi nào trong khắp thế gian, thì người ta cũng sẽ kể lại việc cô ấy đã làm và nhớ đến cô."
vi.R: Ta nói thật với các con: Tin Lành sẽ được rao giảng khắp nơi trên thế giới. Và ở bất cứ nơi nào Tin Lành được rao giảng, người ta sẽ kể lại việc người phụ nữ này đã làm, và họ sẽ nhớ đến cô."

ko.L: 진실로 너희에게 말한다. 온 세상 어디서든지 복음이 선포되는 곳에서는, 이 여자가 한 일도 이야기되어 그 여자를 기억하게 될 것이다."
ko.B: 진실로 너희에게 말한다. 온 세상 어디서든지 복음이 전파되는 곳마다, 사람들이 이 여자가 한 일을 이야기하며 그 여자를 기억할 것이다."
ko.R: 내가 분명히 말한다. 기쁜 소식이 온 세상에 전해질 것이다. 그 소식이 전해지는 곳마다, 사람들은 이 여자가 한 일도 이야기하고 이 여자를 기억할 것이다."

es.L: Y en verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo: dondequiera que se proclame el evangelio en todo el mundo, también lo que esta hizo será contado para memoria de ella».
es.B: En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que en cualquier lugar del mundo entero donde se proclame el evangelio, se contará lo que ella ha hecho, y será recordada».
es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo la verdad: la buena noticia se anunciará en todo el mundo. Y en todas partes donde se anuncie, la gente contará lo que hizo esta mujer, y la recordarán».

fr.L: Et en vérité, je vous le dis : partout où l’Évangile sera proclamé dans le monde entier, ce qu’elle a fait sera aussi raconté en mémoire d’elle. »
fr.B: En vérité, je vous le dis : partout où l’Évangile sera proclamé, dans le monde entier, on racontera aussi ce qu’elle a fait, et on se souviendra d’elle. »
fr.R: Je vous le dis, c’est la vérité : la bonne nouvelle sera annoncée dans le monde entier. Et partout où on l’annoncera, on racontera ce que cette femme a fait, et on se souviendra d’elle. »

sw.L: Na kweli nawaambia, popote Injili itakapohubiriwa katika ulimwengu wote, na hiki alichokifanya huyu kitasimuliwa kwa ukumbusho wake."
sw.B: Kweli nawaambia, kila mahali katika ulimwengu wote ambapo Injili itahubiriwa, watu watasimulia alichofanya mwanamke huyu, na kumkumbuka."
sw.R: Nawaambia ukweli: Habari Njema itahubiriwa katika ulimwengu wote. Na kila mahali itakapohubiriwa, watu watasimulia kile mwanamke huyu alichofanya, nao watamkumbuka."

pt.L: E em verdade eu lhes digo: onde quer que o evangelho seja proclamado, no mundo inteiro, também o que esta [mulher] fez será contado em memória dela."
pt.B: Em verdade eu lhes digo: em qualquer lugar do mundo inteiro onde o evangelho for proclamado, as pessoas vão contar o que ela fez e se lembrarão dela."
pt.R: Eu garanto a vocês: as boas-novas vão ser anunciadas no mundo inteiro. E em todo lugar onde elas forem anunciadas, as pessoas vão contar o que esta mulher fez. Elas vão se lembrar dela."

am.L: ደግሞም እውነት እላችኋለሁ፣ በዓለም ሁሉ ወንጌል በሚሰበክበት ስፍራ ሁሉ ይህች [ሴት] ያደረገችውም ለመታሰቢያዋ ይነገራል።»
am.B: እውነት እላችኋለሁ፣ በዓለም ሁሉ ወንጌል በሚሰበክበት ቦታ ሁሉ፣ እርሷ እንድትታወስ ሰዎች ያደረገችውን ይናገራሉ።»
am.R: እውነቱን እነግራችኋለሁ። የምሥራቹ በዓለም ሁሉ ይሰበካል። በሚሰበክበትም ቦታ ሁሉ ሰዎች ይህች ሴት ያደረገችውን ይናገራሉ። ያስታውሷታልም።»

decisions.choice: the gospel: the good news about Jesus
alternatives: one of the four written Gospels
decisions.reason: As in 1:1 and 13:10, the word means the message about Jesus, not a book.

decisions.choice: will be spoken: will be told
decisions.reason: The passive leaves open who tells it; those who proclaim the gospel will tell her story with it.

decisions.choice: for a memorial of her: so that she is remembered
alternatives: a memorial before God, like an offering
decisions.reason: The word can mean an offering that reminds God (Acts 10:4), but here it means that people will remember her.

decisions.choice: Truly I tell you (B); I tell you the truth (R)
decisions.reason: The same forms as elsewhere in Mark.

decisions.choice: "Thật vậy, Ta nói với các con" (L, B); "Ta nói thật với các con" (R), for the chapter; "Tin Lành" at every level
decisions.reason: The Vietnamese John's form for "Truly", recorded once for this chapter (also 14:18, 14:25, 14:30). "Tin Lành" for the gospel is kept at Readable, as in 13:10.

decisions.choice: "진실로 너희에게 말한다" (L, B); "내가 분명히 말한다" (R), through chapter 14 (14:9, 18, 25, 30)
decisions.reason: As at Mark 3:28 and 13:30, the single form of the Korean John's "진실로 진실로"; modern endings replace the archaic "이르노니". At 14:30 Jesus speaks to Peter alone: "너에게".

decisions.choice: "복음" (L, B); "기쁜 소식" (R)
decisions.reason: Gospel is a key term: "복음" at Literal and Balanced, "기쁜 소식" at Readable, as at 13:10.

decisions.choice: En verdad les digo (L, B); Les digo la verdad (R); evangelio (L, B), buena noticia (R)
decisions.reason: Mark's single "Truly", in the words the Spanish of John uses for its double form; this holds throughout Mark (14:18, 25, 30). Readable says "buena noticia" for "evangelio", as elsewhere in Spanish.

decisions.choice: En vérité, je vous le dis (L, B; "je te le dis" to one person, 14:30); Je vous le dis, c’est la vérité (R); the same in 14:18, 25, 30
alternatives: Je vous le dis en vérité
decisions.reason: The single "Truly" of Mark, in the forms the French of John uses for the double one (French brief, section 5), as in 13:30.

decisions.choice: l’Évangile (L, B); la bonne nouvelle (R)
alternatives: la bonne nouvelle at every level
decisions.reason: As in 13:10 and the French of the letters: the key term is "l’Évangile" at Literal and Balanced, and Readable says "la bonne nouvelle", as the English Readable says "good news".

decisions.choice: Kweli nawaambia (L, B); Nawaambia ukweli (R)
decisions.reason: Mark's single amen, as in 13:30: John's double amen is 'Kweli kweli nawaambia', so the single one is 'Kweli nawaambia'; Readable says 'I tell you the truth', as in John. The same in 14:18, 14:25 and, to Peter alone, 'Kweli nakuambia' in 14:30.

decisions.choice: Em verdade eu lhes digo (L, B); Eu garanto a vocês (R)
decisions.reason: The settled Portuguese wording for the formula (style section 6), for this chapter; to Peter alone in 14:30 it is "Em verdade eu lhe digo" / "Eu garanto a você".

decisions.choice: "እውነት እላችኋለሁ" (L, B); "እውነቱን እነግራችኋለሁ" (R)
decisions.reason: Jesus's "amen" before his own words means "this is true". "አሜን" in Amharic closes a prayer and would be misheard, so Literal and Balanced say "እውነት እላችኋለሁ" (truly I say to you) and Readable "እውነቱን እነግራችኋለሁ" (I tell you the truth), as in Matthew.

decisions.choice: "ወንጌል" (L, B); "የምሥራች" (good news, R)
decisions.reason: "ወንጌል" is the established word for the gospel, but many readers hear it as the name of a book; Readable says "የምሥራች", the good news itself, as in Matthew.

source.text: Καὶ Ἰούδας Ἰσκαριὼθ ὁ εἷς τῶν δώδεκα ἀπῆλθεν πρὸς τοὺς ἀρχιερεῖς ἵνα αὐτὸν παραδοῖ αὐτοῖς.

records.literal_gloss: And Judas Iscariot, the one of the Twelve, went away to the chief priests so that him he might hand over to them.

en.L: And Judas Iscariot, who was one of the Twelve, went away to the chief priests in order to hand {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over to them.
en.B: Then one of the Twelve, Judas Iscariot, went off to the chief priests to betray {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to them.
en.R: Then Judas Iscariot went to the leading priests. He was one of Jesus' twelve followers. He went to offer to help them arrest Jesus.

vi.L: Và Giu-đa Ích-ca-ri-ốt, là một trong [nhóm] Mười Hai, đi đến các thầy tế lễ cả để nộp {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cho họ.
vi.B: Bấy giờ Giu-đa Ích-ca-ri-ốt, một trong nhóm Mười Hai, đi gặp các thầy tế lễ cả để nộp {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cho họ.
vi.R: Sau đó, Giu-đa Ích-ca-ri-ốt đi gặp các thầy tế lễ cả. Ông ta là một trong mười hai môn đồ của Đức Giê-xu. Ông ta đến để đề nghị giúp họ bắt Đức Giê-xu.

ko.L: 그리고 열둘 가운데 하나인 가룟 유다가 그분을 그들에게 넘겨주려고 대제사장들에게 갔다.
ko.B: 그때 열두 제자 가운데 하나인 가룟 유다가 예수를 배반하여 넘겨주려고 대제사장들을 찾아갔다.
ko.R: 그때 가룟 유다가 대제사장들에게 갔다. 유다는 예수의 열두 제자 가운데 하나였다. 그는 대제사장들이 예수를 붙잡도록 돕겠다고 말하려고 간 것이다.

es.L: Y Judas Iscariote, el que era uno de los Doce, se fue a los principales sacerdotes para entregárselo.
es.B: Entonces Judas Iscariote, uno de los Doce, fue a ver a los jefes de los sacerdotes para entregárselo a traición.
es.R: Entonces Judas Iscariote fue a ver a los jefes de los sacerdotes. Era uno de los doce discípulos de Jesús. Fue a ofrecerles su ayuda para arrestar a Jesús.

fr.L: Et Judas Iscariote, celui qui était l’un des Douze, s’en alla vers les chefs des prêtres afin de {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} leur livrer.
fr.B: Alors l’un des Douze, Judas Iscariote, alla trouver les chefs des prêtres pour {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} leur livrer.
fr.R: Alors Judas Iscariote est allé trouver les chefs des prêtres. C’était un des douze disciples de Jésus. Il voulait les aider à arrêter Jésus.

sw.L: Na Yuda Iskariote, yule mmoja wa wale Kumi na Wawili, alienda kwa wakuu wa makuhani ili amkabidhi kwao.
sw.B: Kisha mmoja wa wale Kumi na Wawili, Yuda Iskariote, alienda kwa wakuu wa makuhani ili amsaliti, amtie mikononi mwao.
sw.R: Kisha Yuda Iskariote alienda kwa viongozi wa makuhani. Yeye alikuwa mmoja wa wanafunzi kumi na wawili wa Yesu. Alienda kuwaambia kwamba angewasaidia kumkamata Yesu.

pt.L: E Judas Iscariotes, o [que era] um dos Doze, foi aos chefes dos sacerdotes para entregá-{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} a eles.
pt.B: Então um dos Doze, Judas Iscariotes, foi aos chefes dos sacerdotes, disposto a trair Jesus e entregá-{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} a eles.
pt.R: Então Judas Iscariotes foi falar com os chefes dos sacerdotes. Ele era um dos doze seguidores de Jesus. Ele foi oferecer ajuda para que eles prendessem Jesus.

am.L: ከአሥራ ሁለቱ አንዱ የሆነው የአስቆሮቱ ይሁዳም ለእነርሱ አሳልፎ ሊሰጠው ወደ ካህናት አለቆች ሄደ።
am.B: ከዚያም ከአሥራ ሁለቱ አንዱ የሆነው የአስቆሮቱ ይሁዳ ኢየሱስን አሳልፎ ሊሰጣቸው ወደ ካህናት አለቆች ሄደ።
am.R: ከዚያም የአስቆሮቱ ይሁዳ ወደ ካህናት አለቆች ሄደ። እርሱ ከአሥራ ሁለቱ ደቀ መዛሙርት አንዱ ነበር። ኢየሱስን እንዲይዙት ሊረዳቸው ፈልጎ ሄደ።

decisions.choice: hand over: give Jesus up to his enemies, a betrayal by a friend
decisions.reason: The verb means to hand over, and it is the word Jesus used of his own coming death (9:31; 10:33). When Judas is the subject, it means betrayal.

decisions.choice: the one of the Twelve: one of the Twelve, as everyone knew
decisions.reason: The article may point to him as the one already known from 3:19. Mark stresses that the betrayer was one of Jesus' closest followers.

decisions.choice: hand over (L); betray (B); help them arrest (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the word that links this to Jesus' sayings about being handed over. Balanced and Readable name the betrayal.

decisions.choice: "nộp" (L, B); "giúp họ bắt" (R); "phản bội" (B, R) where no one is named to receive him (14:11, 14:18, 14:21, 14:42, 14:44)
decisions.reason: Vietnamese "phản bội" (betray) cannot take the people he is handed to, so Balanced keeps "nộp ... cho họ" here and uses "phản bội" elsewhere, as the English uses "betray". Literal keeps "nộp" throughout, as the Vietnamese John does.

decisions.choice: "[nhóm] Mười Hai" (L); "nhóm Mười Hai" (B); "mười hai môn đồ" (R)
decisions.reason: Vietnamese needs a noun with the number; "nhóm" (group) keeps "the Twelve" as a name. Judas is "ông ta" in the narrative, a neutral pronoun, since "Giu-đa" is named so often.

decisions.choice: "넘겨주다" (L); "배반하다", "배반하여 넘겨주다" (B, R) for paradidomi of Judas, through chapter 14
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the verb Mark uses for Jesus being handed over (9:31; 10:33; 14:41), as the Korean John does; Balanced and Readable say it was a betrayal by a friend, as the English does. "팔다" (sell), the familiar word of older versions, says more than the Greek.

decisions.choice: "열둘" (L); "열두 제자" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in the Korean Mark 4:10: Literal keeps the bare number, and Balanced and Readable name the Twelve with the book's word for disciples, where the English Readable says "followers".

decisions.choice: entregar (L); entregar a traición (B); ayudar a arrestar (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "entregar", the verb Mark uses of Jesus being handed over (9:31; 10:33; 14:41); Balanced adds "a traición" to say that a friend is doing it (meaning decision m1). The same pattern holds in 14:11, 18, 21, 42 and 44.

decisions.choice: los doce discípulos
decisions.reason: As in the Spanish of John 20:24, Readable says who the Twelve were; disciples stay "discípulos" at every level.

decisions.choice: livrer (L, and B here); trahir (B, R) where Judas is called the one who hands Jesus over (14:11, 18, 21, 42, 44); aider à arrêter (R here)
decisions.reason: French "livrer quelqu’un à ses ennemis" already says betrayal, so Balanced keeps the verb Mark uses for Jesus being handed over (9:31; 10:33) where the sentence names those he is handed to; elsewhere Balanced and Readable say "trahir", as the English says "betray" and the French of John does (18:2). Literal always says "livrer".

decisions.choice: amkabidhi (L); amsaliti (B); angewasaidia kumkamata (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps Mark's verb 'kukabidhi' (hand over), used of John and of Jesus through the book (1:14; 9:31; 10:33; 14:41; 15:1) and again in 14:11, 14:18, 14:21, 14:42-44, so the reader can follow it; Balanced says 'kusaliti' (betray), since a friend hands him over (meaning decision); Readable says what he offered, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: wanafunzi at Readable
decisions.reason: The English Readable of Mark says 'followers'. The Swahili style sheet keeps 'wanafunzi' (disciples) at every level, Readable included, as in John: the word is plain Swahili. The same throughout the chapter.

decisions.choice: entregar (L); trair ... e entregá-lo a eles (B)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "entregar", the verb of Jesus' sayings about being handed over (m1). Portuguese "trair" takes no "to them", so Balanced names the betrayal and keeps "entregá-lo a eles" for the handing over; the same in 14:11, 18, 21, 42 where the English says "betray".

decisions.choice: "አሳልፎ መስጠት" (to hand over) for Judas's act (L, B); "እንዲይዙት ሊረዳቸው" (to help them arrest him, R)
decisions.reason: Mark uses the verb "hand over" for what Judas does and for what happens to Jesus (9:31; 10:33). "አሳልፎ መስጠት" keeps that one word through the chapter and in Amharic already means giving someone up to his enemies, as in Matthew 26:15.

source.text: οἱ δὲ ἀκούσαντες ἐχάρησαν καὶ ἐπηγγείλαντο αὐτῷ ἀργύριον δοῦναι.

records.literal_gloss: And having heard they rejoiced and promised him silver to give.

en.L: And when they heard [it], they rejoiced and promised to give him money.
en.B: They were delighted to hear it and promised to pay him.
en.R: The priests were very happy when they heard this. They promised to give Judas money.

vi.L: Và khi nghe [điều ấy], họ vui mừng và hứa sẽ cho ông ta tiền.
vi.B: Nghe vậy, họ rất mừng và hứa sẽ trả tiền cho ông ta.
vi.R: Các thầy tế lễ rất vui khi nghe điều này. Họ hứa sẽ cho Giu-đa tiền.

ko.L: 그들은 듣고 기뻐하며 그에게 은돈을 주겠다고 약속하였다.
ko.B: 그들은 그 말을 듣고 기뻐하며 유다에게 돈을 주겠다고 약속했다.
ko.R: 대제사장들은 그 말을 듣고 아주 기뻐했다. 그들은 유다에게 돈을 주겠다고 약속했다.

es.L: Y ellos, al oír[lo], se alegraron y prometieron darle dinero.
es.B: Ellos se alegraron mucho al oírlo y prometieron pagarle.
es.R: Los sacerdotes se pusieron muy contentos al oír esto. Prometieron darle dinero a Judas.

fr.L: Et eux, l’ayant entendu, se réjouirent et promirent de lui donner de l’argent.
fr.B: Ils furent ravis de l’entendre et promirent de le payer.
fr.R: Les chefs des prêtres ont été très contents d’entendre cela. Ils ont promis de donner de l’argent à Judas.

sw.L: Nao waliposikia walifurahi, wakaahidi kumpa fedha.
sw.B: Walifurahi sana kusikia hivyo, wakaahidi kumlipa.
sw.R: Viongozi wa makuhani walifurahi sana waliposikia jambo hilo. Wakaahidi kumpa Yuda fedha.

pt.L: E eles, ouvindo [isso], se alegraram e prometeram lhe dar dinheiro.
pt.B: Eles ficaram muito contentes ao ouvir isso e prometeram lhe pagar.
pt.R: Os chefes dos sacerdotes ficaram muito felizes quando ouviram isso. Eles prometeram dar dinheiro a Judas.

am.L: እነርሱም ሰምተው ደስ አላቸው፤ ገንዘብም ሊሰጡት ቃል ገቡለት።
am.B: እነርሱም ይህን ሲሰሙ እጅግ ደስ አላቸው፤ ገንዘብም ሊከፍሉት ቃል ገቡለት።
am.R: የካህናት አለቆቹ ይህን ሲሰሙ በጣም ደስ አላቸው። ለይሁዳ ገንዘብ ሊሰጡት ቃል ገቡ።

decisions.choice: silver: money
decisions.reason: The word means silver and was used of money in general. Matthew 26:15 gives the sum as thirty pieces of silver.

decisions.choice: they rejoiced: the leaders' problem of 14:1-2 is solved
decisions.reason: One of Jesus' own followers offers a way to take him quietly.
The Greek word is "silver", meaning money (meaning decision); Literal keeps the metal in "은돈", which is still a Korean word for money.

decisions.choice: "ገንዘብ" (money) for "silver"
decisions.reason: The word means silver money (m1). "ብር" is also the name of the Ethiopian currency and would make the story sound modern, so Amharic says "ገንዘብ".

source.text: καὶ ἐζήτει πῶς αὐτὸν εὐκαίρως παραδοῖ.

records.literal_gloss: And he was seeking how him conveniently he might hand over.

en.L: And he was seeking how he might conveniently hand {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over.
en.B: So Judas looked for a good chance to betray {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: From then on Judas watched for the right time to hand Jesus over to them.

vi.L: Và ông ta tìm cách nộp {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cho thuận tiện.
vi.B: Vậy Giu-đa tìm dịp thuận tiện để phản bội {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Từ đó, Giu-đa rình chờ đúng lúc để nộp Đức Giê-xu cho họ.

ko.L: 그리고 그는 어떻게 하면 적당한 때에 그분을 넘겨줄 수 있을지 찾고 있었다.
ko.B: 그래서 유다는 예수를 배반하여 넘겨줄 좋은 기회를 엿보았다.
ko.R: 그때부터 유다는 예수를 그들에게 넘겨줄 알맞은 때를 기다렸다.

es.L: Y él buscaba cómo entregarlo en un momento oportuno.
es.B: Así que Judas buscaba una buena ocasión para entregarlo a traición.
es.R: Desde ese momento, Judas buscaba el momento oportuno para entregarles a Jesús.

fr.L: Et il cherchait comment {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} livrer au moment favorable.
fr.B: Judas chercha donc une bonne occasion de {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} trahir.
fr.R: À partir de ce moment, Judas a guetté le bon moment pour leur livrer Jésus.

sw.L: Naye alikuwa akitafuta jinsi atakavyomkabidhi kwa wakati unaofaa.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo Yuda akawa akitafuta nafasi nzuri ya kumsaliti.
sw.R: Tangu wakati huo Yuda alikuwa akivizia wakati unaofaa wa kumtia Yesu mikononi mwao.

pt.L: E ele procurava como entregá-{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} no momento oportuno.
pt.B: Então Judas ficou procurando uma boa oportunidade para {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} trair.
pt.R: Desde então, Judas ficou esperando a hora certa para entregar Jesus a eles.

am.L: እርሱም እንዴት በሚመች ጊዜ አሳልፎ እንደሚሰጠው ይፈልግ ነበር።
am.B: ስለዚህ ይሁዳ እርሱን አሳልፎ የሚሰጥበትን ምቹ ጊዜ ይፈልግ ነበር።
am.R: ከዚያን ጊዜ ጀምሮ ይሁዳ ኢየሱስን ለእነርሱ አሳልፎ የሚሰጥበትን አመቺ ጊዜ ይጠባበቅ ነበር።

decisions.choice: conveniently: at a good moment, when no crowd was near
decisions.reason: The leaders wanted to avoid the crowds (14:2), so Judas looked for a time when Jesus was away from them.

decisions.choice: betray (B); hand ... over to them (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced names the betrayal as in 14:10. Readable spells out to whom he was handed over.

source.text: Καὶ τῇ πρώτῃ ἡμέρᾳ τῶν ἀζύμων, ὅτε τὸ πάσχα ἔθυον, λέγουσιν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ· Ποῦ θέλεις ἀπελθόντες ἑτοιμάσωμεν ἵνα φάγῃς τὸ πάσχα;

records.literal_gloss: And on the first day of the Unleavened [Bread], when the Passover they were sacrificing, say to him the disciples of him, Where do you want having gone we should prepare so that you may eat the Passover?

en.L: And on the first day of Unleavened Bread, when they were sacrificing the Passover [lamb], {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Where do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} want us to go and prepare for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to eat the Passover?"
en.B: On the first day of Unleavened Bread, the day the Passover lambs were sacrificed, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Where would {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} like us to go and make ready for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to eat the Passover meal?"
en.R: It was the first day of the Festival of Unleavened Bread. On this day the lambs were killed for the Passover meal. Jesus' followers said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Where should we go to make the Passover meal ready for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?"

vi.L: Và vào ngày thứ nhất của [Lễ] Bánh Không Men, khi người ta giết [chiên con] Lễ Vượt Qua làm sinh tế, các môn đồ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Thầy muốn chúng con đi chuẩn bị ở đâu để Thầy ăn Lễ Vượt Qua?"
vi.B: Vào ngày thứ nhất của Lễ Bánh Không Men, là ngày người ta giết chiên con Lễ Vượt Qua làm sinh tế, các môn đồ hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Thầy muốn chúng con đi chuẩn bị bữa ăn Lễ Vượt Qua cho Thầy ở đâu?"
vi.R: Hôm ấy là ngày đầu tiên của Lễ Bánh Không Men. Vào ngày này, người ta giết chiên con để ăn bữa Lễ Vượt Qua. Các môn đồ hỏi Đức Giê-xu: "Thầy muốn chúng con đi đâu để chuẩn bị bữa ăn Lễ Vượt Qua cho Thầy?"

ko.L: 그리고 무교절 첫날, 곧 유월절 [양을] 잡는 날에, 그분의 제자들이 그분께 말한다. "저희가 어디로 가서 선생님께서 유월절 [음식을] 잡수시도록 준비하기를 원하십니까?"
ko.B: 무교절 첫날, 곧 유월절 양을 잡는 날에, 제자들이 예수께 말했다. "선생님께서 유월절 음식을 잡수시도록 저희가 어디로 가서 준비하면 좋겠습니까?"
ko.R: 무교절 첫날이었다. 이날에는 유월절 음식을 위하여 양을 잡았다. 제자들이 예수께 여쭈었다. "저희가 어디로 가서 선생님께서 드실 유월절 음식을 준비하면 되겠습니까?"

es.L: Y el primer día de los [Panes] sin Levadura, cuando sacrificaban el [cordero de la] Pascua, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dicen {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos: «¿Dónde quieres que vayamos a preparar[la] para que comas la Pascua?».
es.B: El primer día de la fiesta de los Panes sin Levadura, cuando se sacrificaban los corderos de la Pascua, {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijeron: «¿Dónde quieres que vayamos a prepararte la cena de Pascua?».
es.R: Era el primer día de la fiesta de los Panes sin Levadura. Ese día se mataban los corderos para la cena de Pascua. Los discípulos de Jesús {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntaron: «¿Dónde quieres que vayamos a preparar la cena de Pascua para {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}?».

fr.L: Et le premier jour des Pains sans levain, quand on sacrifiait [l’agneau de] la Pâque, {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} disent : « Où veux-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} que nous allions faire les préparatifs pour que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} manges la Pâque ? »
fr.B: Le premier jour des Pains sans levain, le jour où l’on sacrifiait les agneaux de la Pâque, {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dirent : « Où veux-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} que nous allions {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} préparer le repas de la Pâque ? »
fr.R: C’était le premier jour de la fête des Pains sans levain. Ce jour-là, on tuait les agneaux pour le repas de la Pâque. Les disciples de Jésus {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ont demandé : « Où veux-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} que nous allions préparer le repas de la Pâque pour {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} ? »

sw.L: Na siku ya kwanza ya [Sikukuu ya] Mikate Isiyotiwa Chachu, walipokuwa wakichinja [mwanakondoo wa] Pasaka, wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wanamwambia, "Unataka twende wapi tukuandalie upate kula Pasaka?"
sw.B: Siku ya kwanza ya Sikukuu ya Mikate Isiyotiwa Chachu, siku ambayo wanakondoo wa Pasaka walichinjwa, wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walimwuliza, "Ungependa twende wapi tukuandalie chakula cha Pasaka ule?"
sw.R: Ilikuwa siku ya kwanza ya Sikukuu ya Mikate Isiyotiwa Chachu. Siku hiyo wanakondoo walichinjwa kwa ajili ya chakula cha Pasaka. Wanafunzi wa Yesu walimwuliza, "Tuende wapi tukakuandalie chakula cha Pasaka?"

pt.L: E, no primeiro dia dos [Pães] sem Fermento, quando sacrificavam o [cordeiro da] Páscoa, os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} discípulos {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} dizem: "Onde queres que vamos e preparemos para que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} comas a Páscoa?"
pt.B: No primeiro dia da festa dos Pães sem Fermento, o dia em que se sacrificavam os cordeiros da Páscoa, os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} discípulos {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} perguntaram: "Aonde queres que vamos para preparar a ceia da Páscoa para {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}?"
pt.R: Era o primeiro dia da festa dos Pães sem Fermento. Nesse dia os cordeiros eram mortos para a ceia da Páscoa. Os seguidores de Jesus perguntaram a {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}: "Aonde devemos ir para preparar a ceia da Páscoa para {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}?"

am.L: የፋሲካንም [በግ] በሚያርዱበት በቂጣ [በዓል] የመጀመሪያ ቀን ደቀ መዛሙርቱ፦ «ሄደን ፋሲካን ትበላ ዘንድ የት እንድናዘጋጅልህ ትወዳለህ?» ይሉታል።
am.B: የፋሲካ በጎች በሚታረዱበት በቂጣ በዓል የመጀመሪያ ቀን ደቀ መዛሙርቱ፦ «የፋሲካን ራት እንድትበላ ሄደን የት እንድናዘጋጅልህ ትፈልጋለህ?» አሉት።
am.R: እርሾ ያልገባበት ቂጣ የሚበላበት በዓል የመጀመሪያ ቀን ነበር። በዚህ ቀን ለፋሲካ ራት በጎች ይታረዱ ነበር። ደቀ መዛሙርቱ ኢየሱስን እንዲህ አሉት፦ «የፋሲካን ራት የት ሄደን እንድናዘጋጅልህ ትፈልጋለህ?»

decisions.choice: say: present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: As often in Mark, past events are told in the present tense to make them vivid. The sense is past: they asked. Mark does the same many times in this chapter.

decisions.choice: the first day ... when they sacrificed the Passover: 14 Nisan
alternatives: 15 Nisan, the day after the meal
decisions.reason: The lambs were killed in the temple on the afternoon of 14 Nisan and eaten that evening, when 15 Nisan began. People also spoke of 14 Nisan as the first day of the festival, because all yeast was removed from houses that day.

decisions.choice: the Passover: the Passover meal, with its lamb
decisions.reason: Here the word means the meal, as "eat the Passover" shows.

decisions.choice: the Passover meal
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that the meal is meant.

decisions.choice: "Thầy" for "you" and "chúng con" for "we", with no setting span; Literal keeps the historic present "nói"
alternatives: "{{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}" where the English has a deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: Disciples speak to Jesus as their teacher (style guide section 6); "Thầy" is a noun of address, always capitalised, and takes no setting. The same holds for Peter in 14:29-31.

decisions.choice: "선생님께서 ... 잡수시도록" for "you ... eat"
decisions.reason: Korean does not say "you" to a teacher; the disciples name him "선생님" and use the honorific verb for eating, in 합쇼체 (style guide, section 4).

decisions.choice: 유월절 [양을] 잡는; 유월절 [음식을] (L)
decisions.reason: The Greek says "sacrifice the Passover" and "eat the Passover", meaning the lamb and the meal (meaning decision); Korean needs the noun, which Literal brackets.

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal (dice, envía, viene, toma); pretérito at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: Literal keeps Mark's present (meaning decision m1); Balanced and Readable use the pretérito, as Spanish tells a story. This applies throughout the chapter.

decisions.choice: para {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}
decisions.reason: The stressed "ti" for Christ takes the setting; the verbs addressed to him ("quieres", "comas") need no pronoun in Spanish.

decisions.choice: les disciples at every level, Readable included
decisions.reason: The French brief keeps "disciples" at every level, as the French of John does; the word is familiar in French, where the English Readable says "followers". The same through the chapter (14:13, 16, 17, 20, 32, 37, 43, 50, 69, 70).

decisions.choice: historic present kept at Literal (wanamwambia); past at Balanced and Readable (walimwuliza)
decisions.reason: Mark tells some past events in the present tense (meaning decision on 'say'). Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable use the narrative past, with -ka- for verbs that follow. This holds for the whole chapter (14:13, 17, 27, 30, 32-34, 37, 41, 43, 45, 51, 53, 63, 66-67).

decisions.choice: a ceia da Páscoa
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 26:17: "ceia" is the Portuguese word for an evening meal and the one used for this supper. The disciples speak to Jesus with "tu" ("queres", "para ti").

decisions.choice: "የፋሲካን [በግ] በሚያርዱበት" (when they slaughtered the Passover [lamb], L); "ይሉታል" (say to him, L); "ደቀ መዛሙርት" at Readable too
decisions.reason: "The Passover" that was sacrificed is the lamb (m3), which Literal supplies in brackets and keeps Mark's present "say" (m1). As in Matthew, the disciples are "ደቀ መዛሙርት" at every level, where the English Readable says "followers" (docs/amharic-style.md, section 7b).

source.text: καὶ ἀποστέλλει δύο τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ὑπάγετε εἰς τὴν πόλιν, καὶ ἀπαντήσει ὑμῖν ἄνθρωπος κεράμιον ὕδατος βαστάζων· ἀκολουθήσατε αὐτῷ, καὶ ὅπου ἐὰν εἰσέλθῃ εἴπατε τῷ οἰκοδεσπότῃ ὅτι Ὁ διδάσκαλος λέγει· Ποῦ ἐστιν τὸ κατάλυμά μου ὅπου τὸ πάσχα μετὰ τῶν μαθητῶν μου φάγω;

records.literal_gloss: And he sends two of the disciples of him and says to them, Go into the city, and will meet you a man a jar of water carrying; follow him, \v 14 and wherever he enters say to the master of the house that The Teacher says, Where is the guest room of me where the Passover with the disciples of me I may eat?

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sends two of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples and says to them, "Go into the city, and a man carrying a jar of water will meet you. Follow him, \v 14 and wherever he goes in, say to the owner of the house, 'The Teacher says, "Where is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} guest room where I may eat the Passover with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} disciples?"'
en.B: So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sent off two of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples with these instructions: "Go into the city. A man carrying a water jar will come to meet you. Follow him, \v 14 and when he goes into a house, tell the owner of the house, 'The Teacher says, "Which is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} guest room, where I am to eat the Passover with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} disciples?"'
en.R: Jesus sent two of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers into Jerusalem. He told them, "Go into the city. You will meet a man who is carrying a jar of water. Follow him. \v 14 He will go into a house. Say to the owner of that house, 'The Teacher wants to know, "Where is the room for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to stay in? I want to eat the Passover meal there with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} followers."'

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sai hai môn đồ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi và nói với họ: "Hãy vào thành, và một người đàn ông mang một vò nước sẽ gặp các con; hãy đi theo người ấy, \v 14 và người ấy vào nhà nào, hãy nói với chủ nhà rằng: 'Thầy nói: "Phòng khách của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, nơi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ăn Lễ Vượt Qua với các môn đồ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, ở đâu?"'
vi.B: Vậy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sai hai môn đồ đi và dặn họ: "Hãy vào thành. Sẽ có một người đàn ông mang vò nước đến gặp các con. Hãy đi theo người ấy. \v 14 Người ấy vào nhà nào, hãy nói với chủ nhà đó: 'Thầy hỏi: "Phòng khách của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ở đâu, nơi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ ăn Lễ Vượt Qua với các môn đồ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}?"'
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu sai hai môn đồ vào Giê-ru-sa-lem. Ngài dặn họ: "Hãy vào thành. Các con sẽ gặp một người đàn ông đang mang một vò nước. Hãy đi theo người ấy. \v 14 Người ấy sẽ vào một ngôi nhà. Hãy nói với chủ nhà đó: 'Thầy muốn hỏi: "Căn phòng dành cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ở đâu? Ta muốn ăn bữa Lễ Vượt Qua tại đó với các môn đồ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}."'

ko.L: 그러자 그분이 그분의 제자들 가운데 두 사람을 보내시며 그들에게 말씀하신다. "성 안으로 가거라. 그러면 물 항아리를 지고 가는 사람이 너희를 만날 것이다. 그를 따라가거라. \v 14 그리고 그가 어디로 들어가든지, 그 집 주인에게 '선생님께서 말씀하십니다. "내가 내 제자들과 함께 유월절 [음식]을 먹을 내 객실이 어디 있느냐?"' 하고 말하여라.
ko.B: 예수께서 제자 두 사람을 보내시며 이렇게 이르셨다. "성 안으로 들어가거라. 물 항아리를 메고 가는 남자를 만날 것이니, 그 사람을 따라가거라. \v 14 그가 어느 집에 들어가거든, 그 집 주인에게 '내가 제자들과 함께 유월절 음식을 먹을 객실이 어디 있느냐고 선생님께서 물으십니다' 하고 말하여라.
ko.R: 예수께서 제자 두 사람을 예루살렘으로 보내시며 말씀하셨다. "성 안으로 들어가거라. 물 항아리를 들고 가는 남자를 만날 것이다. 그 사람을 따라가거라. \v 14 그 사람이 어떤 집으로 들어갈 것이다. 그 집 주인에게 '선생님께서 물어보라고 하셨습니다. "내가 제자들과 함께 유월절 음식을 먹을 방이 어디 있느냐?"' 하고 말하여라.

es.L: Y envía a dos de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos y les dice: «{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} a la ciudad, y {{plural_you:les|os}} saldrá al encuentro un hombre que lleva un cántaro de agua; {{plural_you:síganlo|seguidlo}}, \v 14 y dondequiera que entre, {{plural_you:digan|decid}} al dueño de la casa: “El Maestro dice: ‘¿Dónde está {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} cuarto de huéspedes, donde pueda comer la Pascua con {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} discípulos?’”.
es.B: Así que envió a dos de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos con estas instrucciones: «{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} a la ciudad. {{plural_you:Les|Os}} saldrá al encuentro un hombre que lleva un cántaro de agua. {{plural_you:Síganlo|Seguidlo}}, \v 14 y cuando entre en una casa, {{plural_you:díganle|decidle}} al dueño de la casa: “El Maestro pregunta: ‘¿Cuál es {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} cuarto de huéspedes, donde he de comer la Pascua con {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} discípulos?’”.
es.R: Jesús envió a dos de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos a Jerusalén. Les dijo: «{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} a la ciudad. {{plural_you:Se encontrarán|Os encontraréis}} con un hombre que lleva un cántaro de agua. {{plural_you:Síganlo|Seguidlo}}. \v 14 Va a entrar en una casa. {{plural_you:Díganle|Decidle}} al dueño de esa casa: “El Maestro quiere saber: ‘¿Dónde está la sala donde puedo quedarme? Quiero comer allí la cena de Pascua con {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} discípulos’”.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} envoie deux de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples et leur dit : « Allez dans la ville, et un homme portant une cruche d’eau viendra à votre rencontre ; suivez-le, \v 14 et là où il entrera, dites au maître de maison : “Le Maître dit : Où est {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} salle, où je mangerai la Pâque avec {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} disciples ?”
fr.B: Il envoya donc deux de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples avec ces instructions : « Allez à la ville. Un homme qui porte une cruche d’eau viendra à votre rencontre. Suivez-le \v 14 et, quand il entrera dans une maison, dites au propriétaire : “Le Maître te fait dire : Où est la salle qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}est réservée, où je mangerai la Pâque avec {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} disciples ?”
fr.R: Jésus a envoyé deux de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples à Jérusalem. Il leur a dit : « Allez dans la ville. Vous allez rencontrer un homme qui porte une cruche d’eau. Suivez-le. \v 14 Il va entrer dans une maison. Dites au propriétaire de cette maison : “Le Maître demande : Où est la salle pour {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ? Je veux y manger le repas de la Pâque avec {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} disciples.”

sw.L: Naye anawatuma wawili wa wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} na kuwaambia, "Nendeni mjini, na mwanamume atakutana nanyi akibeba mtungi wa maji. Mfuateni, \v 14 na popote atakapoingia, mwambieni mwenye nyumba, 'Mwalimu anasema, "Kiko wapi chumba {{deity_pronoun:changu|Changu}} cha wageni, ambamo nitakula Pasaka pamoja na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}?"'
